creem.activation_decision_2026-09-05: NOT activating now, despite approval. Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/checkout infrastructure -- the same job Stripe already does live for this experiment (prod_V8TDzCnDU7y2r9, $19, Managed Payments + automatic tax). Approval removes the 'is it usable' uncertainty but does not create a Net-Profit case on its own: no buyer would newly discover the product through Creem (it has no marketplace/search surface, unlike Etsy or Gumroad), so building it would only offer existing buyers a second checkout for the same product -- pure substitution, not incremental reach. Building it now would cost real AI-compute (product config, checkout integration, workflow, docs, cost-ledger wiring) for zero expected incremental revenue, while Etsy (validated buyer search-intent, going live this same iteration) and watching Gumroad/Etsy for a first sale are both higher-expected-value uses of the same budget. Would reconsider only if a specific advantage over Stripe surfaces (e.g. materially lower fees, a market/currency Stripe can't serve, or a partner/embed distribution channel unique to Creem) -- none identified as of this decision.
creem.assessment: Even with account + API + approval all confirmed, Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/billing infrastructure -- functionally the same job Stripe already does live, not a marketplace with its own buyer-search discovery. No distribution-value differentiator over Stripe has been identified. Deprioritized: approved and usable, but NOT being activated absent a specific identified advantage (would be redundant payment infra).
